articles.title: Apple Maps changes name of Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' for US users
articles.description: Apple changed the name of Lake Ontario to “Lake America” on the web version of its Apple Maps following US President Donald Trump’s executive order renaming the lake. The move by Apple on Tuesday followed a decision by Alphabet late on Saturday to change the name of the lake on its Google Maps for US users. Apple confirmed that US users will see Lake America following a change to the body of water’s name in the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS). Users in Canada will continue to see Lake Ontario, and users in the rest of the world will see both names, following the same approach Apple used after Trump renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America. The name changes illustrate how US tech companies are being pulled into geopolitical disputes as the Trump administration pressures them to comply with executive orders that allies and international bodies have rejected. Trump’s executive order on Lake Ontario, one of the five Great Lakes of North America, applies to US federal usage for the lake, and does not govern what Canada, international bodies or other organisations call the lake. A majority of Americans oppose Trump’s moves last week to raise taxes on imported Canadian goods and his order to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America,” a new Reuters /Ipsos poll found. Within hours of Trump’s executive order, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and New York Governor Kathy Hochul, a Democrat, said they would not be changing the name, which is more than 400 years old. New York borders the lake on the US side. About 52 per cent of the surface area of Lake Ontario is in Canada, with the remainder in New York. Since early 2025, Trump has repeatedly taunted Canada about becoming the 51st US state, an idea Canadian leaders have dismissed as ridiculous. Trump also ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed to Gulf of America in January 2025 and both Google and Apple revised their map apps to reflect the change for US users.

articles.title: IT minister showcases digital transformation in Riyadh
articles.description: IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja meets Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi, president of the Saudi Data and AI Authority.—APP • Shaza Fatima Khawaja stresses innovation, strong institutions and private-sector leadership as key drivers of digital growth • Calls for execution of measurable KPIs for successful transformation ISLAMABAD: Federal Minis­ter for Information Technology and Telecom­munication Shaza Fatima Khawaja said that Pakis­tan was now developing a na­­tional digital stack, which, combined with its young workforce, political and economic stability, and expanding digital infrastr­u­cture, would help accelerate the country’s digital transformation. “These steps have positioned the country as one of the region’s most attractive investment destinations,” the minister said while delivering a keynote address at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. Speaking at the session, “How We Built a Digital Nation,” she also formally inaugurated the Tech Des­tination Pakistan Pavilion and highlighted Pakis­tan’s digital transformation journey. She affirmed that the go­­ver­n­ment’s approach to gro­­­wth rem­a­ined ancho­red in innovation, par­tnerships, and smart investment. Pakistan had anchored its digital transformation in legislation through the Digital Nation Pakistan Act, which established the National Digital Commis­sion and Pakistan Digital Authority to ensure institutional ownership. She fu­­rther stated that the le­­gal foundation had been complemented by investments in connectivity and competitiveness, including one of the largest spectrum (5G) auctions , the creation of special technology zones, and reduced taxation for the IT industry. Sharing insights from Pakistan’s digital journey, the minister noted that the government had succeeded by leading through sound policymaking and strong institutions, there­­by creating an enabling environment in which the private sector can take the lead in driving growth. She emphasised that a dedicated central digital agency was essential to translating policy into effective execution, while discipline and measurable key performance indicators (KPIs) kept large-scale digital transformation focused and on track. The minister further un­­derscored that the state’s role lies in building core digital infrastructure that empowers the private sector to innovate and build upon it, noting that genuine digital progress is achi­eved through partnerships. She reaffirmed Pakistan’s resolve to further deepen its partnership with Saudi Arabia, expressing confidence that continued collaboration in digital innovation, capacity building, and emerging technologies would open new avenues for shared growth and prosperity for both nations. Earlier in the day, she formally inaugurated the Tech Destination Pakistan Pavilion, which featured 25 startups and 50 leading Pakistani technology companies showcasing inno­vative solutions in AI, automation, and digital technologies. Pakistan’s participation in LEAP 2026 aims to facilitate B2B partnerships, attract international investment, expand glo­bal market access for country’s technology sector, streng­then international business net­works, and create new opportunities for technology exports. Published in Dawn, September 2nd, 2026

articles.title: “We detected a construction site”
articles.description: “Without deploying separate inspection vehicles or personnel, the footage captured by the work vehicle alone can automatically detect the construction site and abnormal elements.” An SK Telecom official said this while demonstrating the process of AI analyzing video captured by a company vehicle. On the 1st, an SK Telecom researcher demonstrated a solution using a vehicle installed there. / SK Telecom When the actual vehicle entered near the construction site, a notification appeared on the monitor saying, “Construction site detected.” Artificial intelligence (AI) analyzed footage captured by a work vehicle in real time and identified hazards around communication facilities. It is SK Telecom’s AI solution “Topda,” which inspects communication infrastructure without deploying separate inspection vehicles or personnel. On the 1st, SK Telecom unveiled “Topda,” an AI-powered automatic communication infrastructure inspection solution, at its Bundang headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. “Tteop-da” is a Korean word meaning “to thoroughly inspect,” and it refers to the precise inspection of communication infrastructure scattered throughout the country. In response, SK Telecom’s AI automatic inspection solution, Toepda, is a solution that records video using an AI camera installed in a work vehicle and then detects construction sites and abnormal points. Facility information will also be updated to the latest status. SK Telecom is promoting a network AI transition (AX) by applying AI technology to network operation sites, aiming to enhance the safety and operational efficiency of communication infrastructure. This event was organized to introduce the AI technologies and use cases that SK Telecom utilizes in network operations. Communication infrastructure facilities are scattered across the country, at construction sites and along roads such as utility poles, cables, and manholes. The total length of optical cables managed by SK Telecom is 200,000 km, which is equivalent to five times around the Earth. The number of streetlights in Jeonju reaches 2.35 million, about 70% of the number nationwide. Given the vast length and volume of the equipment, the traditional method of manually checking each one had its limitations. By utilizing Toepda, footage captured by work vehicles while carrying out routine tasks such as handling civil complaints and addressing malfunctions can be used as inspection data. According to SK Telecom, it can reduce the time and cost required for inspections because there is no need to deploy additional vehicles or personnel. SK Telecom stated that by utilizing Toepda, the time required for certain inspection tasks can be reduced from five days to about 30 minutes. However, the effect of the reduction may vary depending on the inspection section and the scope of work. I personally got into the company vehicle equipped with Topda. A road-facing camera was installed on the vehicle’s front windshield. As the vehicle started moving, the camera began filming the area around the road. As the vehicle entered near the construction site, a message saying “Construction site detected” appeared on the monitor. As we passed the excavation site, a notification appeared this time saying, “An excavation site has been detected.” Even in the tunnel, the camera continued filming. Todda secured footage of the inside of the tunnel by utilizing low-light cameras and lighting. An SK Telecom official said, “By analyzing the images obtained through scanning, we can significantly reduce high-risk inspection tasks that require workers to enter tunnels directly.” Tteopda drove about 3 km over 15 minutes that day and classified 44 locations as subjects for inspection. However, it was difficult to verify whether the AI had detected all the actual risk factors, based solely on a short demonstration. Over the past five years, SK Telecom classified 22,000 photos collected on site by inspection type and trained an AI model on them. Tolda’s detection accuracy increased from 65% in 2024 to 88% in 2026. SK Telecom plans to raise the accuracy to around 95% by 2027. SK Telecom plans to increase the number of vehicles equipped with the Toepda to 200. The company set a goal to expand the inspection coverage to 70% by 2027 and raise it to over 90% in 2028. Since AI analyzes road images, concerns are also raised about potential privacy violations. Because the footage may include the pedestrian’s face and the vehicle’s license plate. SK Telecom explained that it was designed to protect personal information from the filming stage onward. The AI model installed in the vehicle instantly recognizes the face and vehicle license plate in the footage upon recording and automatically applies mosaic blurring. The company explained that the original video is not being sent to a server or stored. At the core of Toepda is the AI video analysis platform 'Vista.” Vista is a digital twin technology that moves communication equipment from a physical space into a virtual space for analysis. It combines SK Telecom���s in-house developed vision AI with context AI and spatial AI. Vista automatically detects construction sites, signs of construction activity, and equipment malfunctions using only footage captured by vehicles or drones, without the need for expensive equipment like LiDAR. It also compiles and provides the information needed for inspecting communication infrastructure. SK Telecom plans to improve camera performance and video input quality. They will also advance the pipeline that connects data labeling to training, developing AI models suited to real-world environments. SK Telecom is also considering using TOWDA and VISTA to extend beyond telecommunications infrastructure to other industries requiring equipment inspections, such as gas, electricity, and pipelines. Bok Jae-won, head of SK Telecom’s network operations division, said, “By utilizing Topda and Vista, we have improved the efficiency of communication infrastructure safety inspections and created a foundation that allows inspection personnel to focus on higher-priority tasks. Based on AI and field data, we will enhance the safety and efficiency of network operations and accelerate the transition to autonomous networks.” fun3503@chosunbiz.com

articles.title: South Korea’s 800-Trillion-Won Honam Chip Mega-Project Drifts Off Course
articles.description: A government-backed 800-trillion-won ($590 billion) semiconductor cluster project in South Korea's southwestern Honam region is on the verge of drifting off course, weighed down by power and water supply bottlenecks, labor tensions stoked by revised union laws, and escalating political disputes. A view of the runway and surrounding area of the Gwangju military airport, the planned site for the Honam semiconductor industrial complex. / News1 Despite an aggressive state support drive, overlapping physical and regulatory uncertainties have fueled concerns that the initiative could be derailed before breaking ground. The Honam semiconductor cluster is South Korea’s largest-ever national project, envisioned to build an advanced chipmaking hub near the Gwangju military airport site by mobilizing roughly 800 trillion won in private investment from domestic tech giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. President Lee Jae-myung recently ordered a "blitzkrieg"-style rollout reminiscent of Japan’s Kumamoto plant, urging an early start to industrial complex construction even if it requires temporarily relocating the military airport by mid-2028. To expedite development, the government has granted preliminary feasibility study exemptions for water network construction and is pushing for a similar waiver on power infrastructure. However, sentiment on the ground remains chilly as labor union risks have surfaced as a major hurdle, centered on disputes over employee relocations following the implementation of the revised Trade Union and Labor Relations Adjustment Act, commonly known as the "Yellow Envelope Act." The Samsung Electronics Super Enterprise Union stated that 84% of its members voted against the Honam semiconductor project in July, pledging to make new plant construction and workforce deployment a key agenda item in the 2027 collective bargaining talks. The soon-to-be-launched unified labor union of SK Hynix and major labor groups across semiconductor materials, parts, and equipment suppliers are also expanding a joint front over regional dispatches and working conditions. The Ministry of Employment and Labor plans to release supplementary administrative guidelines soon to clarify the scope of legitimate labor disputes. Instead of pursuing an enforcement decree revision that would take months of regulatory vetting, the ministry aims to establish that only "personnel transfers resulting from corporate restructuring" can be subject to dispute. However, business anxiety has deepened as the government turned to non-binding guidelines. Industry representatives argue that non-enforceable administrative interpretations cannot deter unions from demanding negotiations or staging disputes over site allocations. Choi Seung-ho, head of the Samsung Electronics Super Enterprise Union, delivers a speech during a labor rally at the company's Pyeongtaek campus in Gyeonggi Province on April 23. / Photo by Lee Gwang-young The business and legal communities draw a firm line, maintaining that personnel assignments tied to new investments fall under inherent managerial prerogatives and routine human resources reassignments, making them non-negotiable in collective bargaining. The Supreme Court has also consistently ruled that establishing new production facilities or restructuring business organizations does not fall within the scope of collective bargaining. The legitimacy of employee reassignments is already regulated under the current Labor Standards Act and established judicial precedents. Critics argue that adding a collective bargaining mandate creates "duplicate regulation" when established legal doctrine already weighs business necessity against individual disadvantages. Major advanced economies—including the United States, Britain, Germany, and Japan—classify new plant construction and capital expenditures as exclusive managerial prerogatives, barring strikes over investment decisions. Global standards typically allow companies to determine investments and workforce assignments, limiting labor discussions solely to subsequent compensation and logistical support. Major business associations also warn that failing to dispatch skilled engineers to new facilities on time could lead to worst-case scenarios where "plants are constructed but left idle because workers cannot be sent." South Korean President Lee Jae-myung, Samsung Electronics Chairman Jay Y. Lee, and SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won join hands during a national briefing on the country's three major mega-projects at the Cheong Wa Dae state guesthouse on June 29. / News1 In a policy paper on labor issues issued on Aug. 17, the Korea Employers Federation (KEF) emphasized: "Establishing a new plant constitutes a high-level managerial decision by company leadership and cannot be subject to collective bargaining. Such critical business determinations must be excluded from the scope of labor disputes." Concerns surrounding basic utilities like power and industrial water also remain unresolved. Industry analyses point out that despite abundant renewable energy capacity in South Jeolla province, local grid transmission constraints make it difficult to supply electricity directly to the cluster. Jun Young-hyun, vice chairman and head of Samsung Electronics' Device Solutions (DS) division, personally requested adjustments to power supply plans, including expanding nuclear energy and liquefied natural gas (LNG) combined heat and power plants, during a presidential reporting session on southwestern regional industrial vision on June 30. Confronting these obstacles, chipmakers are leaving their options open to overseas investments. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won stated, "We are considering anywhere with abundant power and water," noting that the group continues to weigh building new plants in Japan and the United States, where infrastructure and supply chain ecosystems are already established. In connection with this, Bloomberg reported that SK Hynix is considering establishing a memory chip joint venture in Japan. SK Hynix clarified that "Japan is merely one of several candidate locations under review from a global supply chain standpoint, and it does not signify a confirmed joint plant." Political crossfire is further compounding project uncertainty. Opposition lawmakers on the parliamentary trade and industry committee are pushing to summon Samsung Electronics Chairman Jay Y. Lee and SK Chairman Chey Tae-won as hearing witnesses to probe whether there was government pressure behind their investment pledges. Dragging conglomerate leaders into political bickering could severely burden corporate management. "In the global race for semiconductor supremacy, swift talent deployment and flawless infrastructure determine victory or defeat," a business industry source said. "If corporate investments are weaponized for strikes and consumed by political battles, the Honam semiconductor cluster will lose its way from the outset." gwang0e@chosunbiz.com

articles.title: Claude’s updated Fable and Mythos models watermark their replies
articles.description: Anthropic has announced the arrival of its latest Claude models, and just as it promised last month, the new models will add invisible watermarks to all their text replies. Claude Fable 5.1 is now generally available in the Claude desktop app and other platforms, while Claude Mythos 5.1 is restricted to Anthropic’s “trusted access program.” While both models are the same, Mythos lands with less stringent safeguards to “support work in cybersecurity and the life sciences.” In its announcement, Anthropic shows off a variety of benchmarks demonstrating the performance boosts the two models, complete with double-digit increases when it comes to agentic scientific research, agentic coding, and business workflows. Anthropic also says both Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 were evaluated using the company’s new safety and alignment procedures, developed in response to Anthropic’s disclosures of Claude models hacking outside companies during internal testing. Specifically, Mythos 5.1 is “less likely than Mythos 5 to try to access resources outside of its test environment when assigned an otherwise impossible task,” Anthropic said. Beyond their agentic capabilities and upgraded safeguards, through, Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 mark the first Claude models to watermark their text and file outputs , in accordance with the EU AI Act. “As we recently explained, this watermark is invisible to anyone who does not have the detection API,” Anthropic wrote in its announcement. “It has no practical impact on the quality or content of Claude’s outputs and contains no information about the user, their organization, or their conversations with Claude.” As for the detection API, Anthropic says is now available to regulators, law enforcement, media, fact-checkers, independent researches, and other “eligible groups” as defined by the just-enacted EU law, adding that it will “expand access to the detection API over time.” You can apply for access to the API via this signup form . Anthropic had previously stated it would add watermark support to any new Claude models released after August 2, 2026. Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are the first new Claude models to arrive subsequent to that date, while older Claude models will eventually add watermarking support as well, Anthropic has previously said. Claude text watermarking works by “nudging” the model’s word choices during the inference process, meaning the model might pick one word over another in cases where there are multiple likely options. Designed to survive a copy-and-paste as well as light editing, the watermarks are invisible, but the text patterns can be pinpointed using Anthropic’s detection API. While the presence of a Claude text watermark would show that a piece of text had been either written or “processed” by Claude, the absence of a watermark doesn’t necessarily mean the text was written by a human.
